title: Percentages, Part 1: The Idea and an Easy Problem

beats.say: Percent means per hundred. The SAT tests four kinds of percent questions. The first is finding a percent of a number.
The second is computing a percent change. The third is working backward from a changed value to the original. And the fourth is applying successive changes, one after another.
Convert a percent to a decimal by dividing by one hundred. So thirty-five percent is zero point three five.
Increasing by twenty percent is multiplying by one point two. Decreasing by twenty percent is multiplying by zero point eight. Think in multipliers, not in adding the percent.
Successive changes multiply. A twenty percent increase and then a twenty-five percent decrease is one point two times zero point seven five, which is zero point nine, a ten percent net decrease.
Percent change always uses the original value as the base, which means the number you divide by.
To undo a change, divide by the multiplier. If a price is sixty-eight dollars after a fifteen percent discount, the original is sixty-eight divided by zero point eight five, which is eighty dollars.
beats.item: Undo a change: divide by the multiplier

scenes.title: Phrases and multipliers
rows: a is p percent greater than b

beats.say: An increase by p percent has a multiplier of one plus p over one hundred. For example, a fifteen percent increase has a multiplier of one point one five.
A decrease by p percent has a multiplier of one minus p over one hundred. For example, a fifteen percent decrease has a multiplier of zero point eight five.
The phrase a is p percent greater than b means a equals the multiplier times b. So the base is b, the number being compared to.
The part equals the percent over one hundred, times the whole. This is how you find a percent of a number.
The percent change equals the new value minus the old value, divided by the old value, times one hundred.
Easy example. In part A, what percent of seventy-two is eighteen? In part B, an eighty dollar item increases in price by fifteen percent. What's the new price?
To find what percent eighteen is of seventy-two, divide the part by the whole, and then multiply by one hundred. Eighteen is the part, and seventy-two is the whole.
Eighteen divided by seventy-two is zero point two five. This is the decimal form of the percent.
Multiply by one hundred to convert to a percent. Zero point two five times one hundred is twenty-five. So eighteen is twenty-five percent of seventy-two.
A fifteen percent increase has a multiplier of one point one five. So we multiply the old price, eighty, by one point one five.
Eighty times one point one five is ninety-two. So the new price is ninety-two dollars.
Check by finding the increase directly. Fifteen percent of eighty is zero point one five times eighty, which is twelve. Adding twelve to eighty gives ninety-two. Both methods agree.
To recap. Percent means per hundred, so convert percents to decimals by dividing by one hundred.
Think in multipliers. Increase by p percent is one plus p over one hundred, and decrease is one minus p over one hundred.
Check by computing the change directly. In the next video, we work through a medium problem and a hard problem.
